category_title: Students who engage in disruptive behaviors to avoid nonpreferred writing tasks
minimal_context: Mike is at his desk in the second-grade classroom during independent writing time, tasked with writing a paragraph containing a starter sentence, detail sentences, and a conclusion statement.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent writing. Please begin working on your assignment, making sure to include your starter sentence, detail sentences, and a conclusion statement.

STUDENT: (Mike picks up his pencil and begins loudly tapping it on his desk, looking around the room instead of at his paper.)

TUTOR: Mike, please stop tapping and get to work on your writing.

STUDENT: (Mike gets out of his seat without permission and walks across the room to the pencil sharpener.) I need to sharpen my pencil again.

TUTOR: You just sharpened it. Please sit back down and write your starter sentence.

STUDENT: (Mike walks back to his group but does not sit down. He leans over, tapping the student next to him on the shoulder while they are working, and calls out across the room) Hey, what are you writing? I don't want to do this!

options.A: Dictate the paragraph for Mike using adult diction to ensure a correct transcription of the writing assignment during the session.
options.B: Give Mike a simpler task, such as writing a single sentence, if everyone else is writing a full paragraph during the activity.
options.C: Agree with Mike that he is having a rough time with the independent writing assignment during this session.
options.D: Allow escape from the task following independent completion of specified writing components (starter sentence, detail sentences, conclusion statement) within a predetermined time limit and displaying task engagement behaviors.
